articles.title: ‘It’s radical to release a film called Girls Like Girls in this climate’: hitmaker turned director Hayley Kiyoko on sexuality, safety and becoming ‘Lesbian Jesus’
articles.summary: The singer’s hit 2015 single Girls Like Girls was her breakthrough moment and also the first time she felt confident in her sexuality. Now she has directed a film based on the song – a love letter to her 17-year-old self.
body: A lot of Hayley Kiyoko’s teenage summers were spent waiting, bored and pining, as she sat at the computer willing her crush to message her back on AOL instant messenger. Like Coley, the 17-year-old protagonist of Girls Like Girls, the film the pop star has co-written and directed, Kiyoko fell hard for a girl who “put me through my own heartbreak and haunted me for a long time”, she says.

Although the 35-year-old singer became known by fans as “lesbian Jesus” following the release of her breakthrough single Girls Like Girls in 2015 (the film is an extended version of the story first told in the song’s music video), feeling comfortable in her sexuality didn’t actually come until after its release. Her gay identity was, at the time, the topic she was “the most scared of writing about”, and the song’s confident refrain “Girls like girls like boys do, nothing new” came from wanting to “manifest feeling confident”.

Now she has directed a film based on the song – a love letter to her 17-year-old self.

articles.title: How Bassam Tariq pivoted from stalled Blade reboot to new Mahershala Ali thriller: ‘I’m happier I made this movie’
articles.summary: In the film-maker’s Houston-set film, Ali stars as a devout Muslim who moonlights as a vicious hitman. Mahershala Ali is swinging around a blade in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. That’s not a nod to Ali’s previous attachment to Marvel’s Blade.
body: “You are forced to strike with intention when you use a sword,” Tariq says, speaking in a recent interview in Toronto.

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother fearlessly cuts through that tension while capturing what makes those communities so vibrant and inspiring, and searching for a sense of hope in its heartfelt and intimate interrogation of faith and fatherhood. Those themes were especially important to he and Ali, Tariq says.
“We connected on these things while we were on this [other] movie together,” says Tariq, referring to Marvel’s Blade. “You might have heard of it.”

He’s being cheeky. The fallout from the aborted Blade reboot, which Tariq was set to direct, has become an intricate part of Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’s lore. Ali was attached for several years to star as Marvel’s vampire-slayer, once played by Wesley Snipes. He only recently confirmed that the long-delayed reboot is simply not happening.

articles.title: ‘The Good Girls’ Lead Ilse Salas to Star in Quijote Films’ ‘To Die on Your Feet’ (‘Morir de Pie’) a Project Pitched at Iberseries & Platino Industria (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Mexican actress Ilse Salas, winner of Mexico’s Best Actress Ariel Award for “The Good Girls” (“Las niñas bien”), will lead the cast of the Quijote Films wry dramedy “To Die on Your Feet” (“Morir de Pie”), which has been pitched this week at the Iberseries & Platino Industria in Madrid.
body: Salas is among the most acclaimed Mexican actresses of her generation. Aside from bringing home Mexico’s prestigious Ariel Award for “The Good Girls” in 2019, she was nominated for the Ariel for her performances in Alonso Ruizpalacios’ “Güeros” and Abner Benaim’s “Plaza Catedral,” Panama’s shortlisted entry to the 94 th Academy Awards.
“Latin American cinema is the cinema I watch, seek out, make and dream about. Our voice needs to reach farther and we are making it heard,” said Salas.

The dramedy’s trajectory has taken it across the world through a variety of development and co-production programs in such festivals as Marseille, Toulouse, San Sebastián, the Berlinale and Discovery TIFF 2029. It has already been snapped up by Hulu, HBO and Mubi for various territories.
“To Die on Your Feet” also received backing from the Pfeffer del Sur fund of the José Ignacio International Film Festival.

articles.title: ‘A Few Good Men’ on Broadway: Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford and Team Behind Revival on Why It’s ’So Fucking Relevant’ in Trump Era
articles.summary: Aaron Sorkin never truly feels his scripts are finished. “They’re just confiscated,” he says. “There comes a time when someone says, ‘Pencils down.’” So when director Michael Arden proposed the first Broadway revival of “A Few Good Men,” Sorkin saw an opportunity.
body: The concept of a lawless military felt familiar for the cast. “Every time you look at the news,” says Blyth, “you see something about Pete Hegseth’s military — and how it’s going back to this exact time.” Indeed, the only reason Sorkin didn’t set his new draft in the present day is that Guantanamo Bay, the U.S. military base where the play is set, has become a detention facility for migrants, complicating the story.

“I’ve admired this country,” says Blyth, an Englishman who came to the U.S. to study at Juilliard and has led films including “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” and “People We Meet on Vacation.” “To be doing this play, as a person who has chosen to come here, at a time when America is having a reckoning about war and masculinity — I’m loving sorting through Pandora’s box.” This marks Blyth’s Broadway debut, and he rapturizes about the theater in his adopted homeland. “I got the bug when I was really young, and American playwrights — it’s the epitome of great work.”
The current Secretary of Defense comes up again, as Sorkin remarks to Rodriguez that “one of the things [Hegseth] is doing is kicking out women. Hyper-qualified women are gone.”

articles.title: Madison Avenue Makeover: Marketers Face Big Challenges in Bid to Reach Elusive Consumers
articles.summary: Capturing attention — the first job of advertising — has never been so difficult. With consumers distracted by alerts, texts, posts, emails and likes — not to mention the constant churn of daily life — it’s little wonder that more advertisers are breaking tradition and experimenting at a dizzying…
body: Recent financials tell the tale. In the industry’s most recent upfront market, when U.S. media companies tried to sell the bulk of their commercial inventory, ad spending on broadcast TV dropped by approximately 5.3% compared to 2025, according to an analysis by Media Dynamics, a consulting firm that tracks such outlays. Spending on cable TV fell even more, with marketers cutting outlays by 7.7%. Meanwhile, the volume of ad commitments put toward streaming rose a whopping 30%.

Measurement: Advertisers have, for decades, struggled to determine exactly how many people were exposed to a commercial, but that task has become exponentially more difficult in the digital age. Nielsen and a bevy of rival upstarts are all working to find new ways to capture all types of viewing. Still, the market is splintered around various techniques and proprietary audience-tracking systems devised by media giants and the ad community. The absence of a common yardstick to measure success — a la Nielsen ratings and box office receipts — makes it harder to tell if marketers are getting any bang for their bucks.

body: Romo’s departure from CBS Sports may raise more questions than it answers. His exit opens a prime position during the network’s NFL season at a time when that sports has become even more critical to the fortunes of the company soon to be known as Skydance — the parent company formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. articles.summary: Reports that Jon Watts could make a new trilogy about a clan who have already saved and destroyed the galaxy several times over leaves you wishing for a newer world. The Skywalkers: who are they exactly?
body: Deadline reports this week that Lucasfilm has hired Jon Watts to direct the first instalment of a new trilogy continuing the Skywalker saga, written by Simon Kinberg, with Daisy Ridley reportedly being eyed to return as Rey. The films have not yet been greenlit, and there are precious few other details, but Watts does seem an inspired choice, if for no other reason than that he has previously overseen a film – Spider-Man: No Way Home – that was built around the idea that nobody in a long-running franchise needs to remain dead.

articles.title: Horror films like Obsession are shut out of the Golden Globes – unless they pretend to be comedies
articles.summary: Obsession is a terrifying, violent nightmare of lovestruck madness – but the Globes’ rigid awards categories have forced it into an absurd choice. What do this year’s wish-gone-wrong tale Obsession, gross-out transformation bloodbath The Substance, and Jordan Peele’s generational masterpiece Get…
body: They’re also toe-tapping laugh riots. At least that’s what the Golden Globes would have you believe.

The Globes present a conundrum for horror. Its major categories are split into either “drama” or “musical or comedy” and it’s fair to say neither of those is an obvious home for throat-ripping gorefests or white-knuckle ghost-train rides. So if you’re managing an awards push for a hotly tipped horror, what road do you take? The answer, often, is titters and tap-dancing.

But it’s easy to see how this impulse towards category chicanery arises. Traditionally, the drama category is where the big-hitters duke it out. This year, it’s likely to be a straight fight between Christopher Nolan’s exceptional take on The Odyssey and the Spanish LGBTQ+ epic La Bola Negra. That’s not to mention Dune: Part Three, which could ride a Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King-style wave if Denis Villeneuve can bring Frank Herbert’s books to a satisfying conclusion.
points: Obsession is a terrifying, violent nightmare of lovestruck madness – but the Globes’ rigid awards categories have forced it into an absurd choice.

articles.title: Alison Hammond has heart check-up in hospital after leaving TV's This Morning
articles.summary: The host says she is "fine" but getting checked after leaving midway through Friday's This Morning.
body: Alison Hammond went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show, but has assured followers she is "fine".

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was assisted off the set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".
In a video posted from a hospital bed, external on Friday afternoon, Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" during the show but was feeling OK and was undergoing tests.
"I know you're all worried about me," she said. "Honestly, I am fine. First of all, I'm getting my old ticker checked out."

articles.title: Dolly Parton sings Jolene in Welsh in recording released after her death
articles.summary: Parton's niece Jada Star and Welsh singer Bronwen Lewis say the country artist was proud to sing in Welsh.
body: A new version of Dolly Parton's Jolene is set to be released, with parts of the song sung in Welsh by the legendary country artist.
The song was recorded before her death on 25 August, and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis as well as Parton's niece, Jada Star.
In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote more than 3,000 songs.
The single will come out on 9 October, and is the second posthumous release from Parton - who was of Welsh descent.

articles.title: If AMC+’s “Kill Jackie” is a Question, We’ll Take a Stab at It
articles.summary: From the creatives behind “ Killing Eve,” Catherine Zeta-Jones lands on AMC+ with an assassin show that feels like it was Mad Libs-ed into existence. In “Kill Jackie,” Jackie Price (Zeta-Jones) has spent the past 20 years living in luxury, traveling, and selling fine art in the most complex and…
body: Convinced someone from her past is behind the hit, Jackie revives her old instincts and sets out to return the favor. It’s a get-them-before-they-get-her situation. As the killers close in, Jackie discovers the biggest dangers come from the silliest sources, but the demons within are far more deadly.

That will sound lovely to lovers of the genre, but by episode three of this Technicolor vengeance romp (reminiscent of a nose candy bender), it’s clear Guy Ritchie, Quentin Tarantino, and “John Wick” must have teeth marks on them, because they’ve been bitten into. “Kill Jackie” is more derivative than a FUCCI handbag bought on Canal Street in NYC—it looks like the genuine article, but something’s not quite right.
